content.text: Tx Sx b/c airway remodeling of basement membrane (chronic inflam) -> irreversible & thicker -> ↓ diameter -> mucus & spasms further ↓ -> sig airway compromise
CXR: norm, Get if:
Pt ⍉ know trigger                          -    assoc Sx (fever, URI, sick contact, hemoptysis, new prod cough)
Some diff Sx than norm                 -    Hear other adventitious sounds or percussion abnorm
⍉ norm exacerbation -worse         -    ⍉ able to ensure f/u -> r/o pneumonia
CHF
Pertinent Hx: Hx HF, smoke, meds, recent diet, edema (B/L, DVT Hx), calf circumference -1cm diff =doppler
Inspection: scars, tripod, access musc use, abd breathing, nasal flare
Palpation: PMI, pulse grades, edema grades, lifts-heaves-thrills
Percussion: dullness
Ausc: rales in bases -listen to B/L bases 1st -> worsen -> moves up, poss wheezing/rhonchi (cardiac wheeze)
CXR:  -  enlrg aortic arch   -  cardiomegaly    -  diffuse infiltrates  -   coscophrenic angle ⍉ defined     -  BNP, echo
Pleural Effusion
-    Transudate: mostly H2O -> shift osmotic P -> fluid forced into free space      -    Exudate: protein rich w WBC/pus
Pertinent Hx: URI/pneumonia, Hx malig (mediastinal), Hx HF
Inspection: ↓ chest expansion on effusion side
Palpation: ↓ tactile fremitus, trach deviation
Percussion: dullness
Ausc: ↓ breath sounds, poss pleural rub
CXR: Lat decubitus (w effusion down) -> 1mm thickness =20mL pleural fluid
See shift in meniscus, POCUS-great (fluid=darker & easier to see)
Similar to infiltrate but straight line =fluid meniscus
Atelectasis:
partial-complete collapse of alveolar sacs -distal terminal
Pertinent Hx: post surgery, rib frx -MC cause of post-op fever b/c incomplete chest expansion
Ensure good pain mgnt -big breath, watch for pneumonia b/c warm-moist enivro w/o vent-> bacteria
Pulmonary toilet (hygiene): clear mucus & secretions <- cough, deep breaths
Use incentive spirometry: prevent & tx
Inspection: ↓ chest expansion
Percussion: dull over collapse
Ausc: ↓ breath sounds, poss rales or wheezing
CXR: distal lobes -> white following alveoli
Pneumonia
Pertinent Hx: CAP vs HAP, smoke, DM, IS (HIV, chemo, long-term steroids), CV dz, recent abx or hsp or instrumented (aspiration, mucus in airway)
Percussion: ↑ tactile fremitus, dull
Ausc: rhonchi, rales
CXR:     -    Bacterial: unilat, localized, ⍉ coscophrenic angle, ⍉ sharp diaphragm
-    Viral: B/L diffuse infiltrates
Bronchitis
Pertinent Hx: URI, IS, smoke, had b4?, COPD, emphysema, occupational exposure
COPD, bronchiectasis (thickening of lining), chronic bronchitis (cont smoke-irritants), CF (ronchi)
Palpation: poss rib tender from cough
Percussion: dull -consolidation, ↑tactile fremitus, viral poss have 2ndry bacterial, chronic =hypoxia, SOB, fever
Ausc: rhonchi (pre&post-tx), bronchospasm, cont. ↓ pitch wheezing-snoring-gurgle-rumble -poss clear w cough
CXR: thickening of basement membrane off of diff bronchi
Epiglottitis
THROAT EXAM WARNING-⍉ STICK ANYTHING IN MOUTH IF SUS -spasm & close airway-> stoma
Pertinent Hx: peds (⍉ get H-flu vaccine), hx resp exposure, cough, fever, resp distress, cyanosis, restless
Ausc: stridor-squeaky loud noises -very sm airway
CXR: soft tissue lat C-spine: (+) “thumb print sign” (adjust rad exposure to ↑ soft tissue prominence)
Visualize via nostril, red-swollen =stridor
Tx: Iv abx, steroids, ↑ flow O2, prepare to mgn airway
PE whole segment ⍉ getting blood
Pertinent Hx: virchows triad, Hx malig
Percussion: dull
Ausc: ↓ breath sounds
CXR: ineffective, but can get CXR fast then CT -> spiral CT, ⍉ need if no other indications
More effective to screen for conditions that mimic PE
Typical findings:    -    Atelectasis                -    parenchymal infiltrates    -
elev diaphragm -uni or B/L
Lrg hilum      -    cardiomegaly              -    lrg mediastinum               -    pleural effusion
Prom central pulm a. -Fleischner sign  -    Pleural based area- ↑ opacity (hampton’s sign)
Oligemia (westermarks sign -vessel completely blocked off from clot  -     Pulm edema
V-Qscan (easier on kidneys, get BUN, dehydration tests & ensure ⍉ allergies)
pt inhale radioactive & inject radioactive into blood -> want to see in airway & blood
CT: more sensitive & specific                                          -    Wells criteria: +4 =likely
Pneumothorax
Pertinent Hx: Hx chest trauma, connective tissue dz, sig smoke
Inspection: resp distress
Palpation: ⍉ equal chest expansion
Percussion: hyper-resonant, trachea deviation
Ausc: ↓ breath sounds, (-) tactile fremitus, bleb (sm bullae) -> pop in mucosa -> air leak
Coin test: 2 silver dollar -> place subclavicular-> tap coin on coin while ausc -> bell-like = bleb
CXR: collapse lung, poss overexposure of healthy lung
Interstitial Lung Dz
Pertinent Hx: enviro & occupational exposure
Inspection: chronic dry cough, clubbing, cyanosis
Palpation: ↓ chest expansion
Percussion: basilar (low lobe) dullness
Ausc: B/L fine “velcro crackles” @ bases on inspiration
CXR:   -    Reticular: too many lines  -    Nodular: too many dots    -    Reticulonodular: too many lines & dots
COPD
Pertinent Hx: chronic exposure to irritants/toxins, sm airway dz, parenchymal destruction, ↑ mucus prod
airway narrowing, mucociliary dysfunction (nicotine paralyses cilia->↑cough when stop smoking)
Inspection: barrel chest, tracheal distension on inhale
Palpation: ↓ chest expansion, (-) tactile fremitus, accessory musc use
Percussion: hyper-resonance
Ausc: ↓ lung sounds, wheezing, rhonchi, rales
CXR: pulm HTN, ↓distal & ↑prox pulm vasc markings, flat hemidiaphragm (hyperinflation)
Basic Airway Assessment: ABC’s
A: Airway
-does it work? Patent airway?
B: Breathing
-breathing? Chest wall mvt, pt need help breathing?
C: Circulation
-Sx of cyanosis? ok pulse?
Strd Precaution: Gloves, mask & face shield -↑ likelihood of flying resp secretions, cough, vomit, bite, spit
Resp mask prn: concern for airborne dz (TB, COVID)
Basic Maneuvers
Head-tilt/chin-tilt:
ALWAYS CHECK FOR FB -> NO BLIND SWEEP (PUSH FB IN)
No sus neck injury    -    Floppy tongue (no tone) -> obstruct airway
Temp procedure        -    Replaced w airway adjunct unless pt spont ok ventilation
Purpose: move tongue & epiglottis away from P oropharynx -> can block upper airway
open airway (lifts tongue) -> allow spont/assisted ventilation
Technique: hand on forehead->firm P w palm tilts head back->fingers under lower jaw
(near chin)->lift up to bring chin forward
NO PROTECTION FROM VOMITING             -but ⍉ need equipment
Jaw Thrust: use if spinal injury sus,
Airway more important than spinal injury
Temp procedure, replaced w airway adjunct unless pt spont ok ventilation
Technique: hand both sides of pt head, rest elbow on surface that pt on
Grab zygomatic arch (stable) & pull forward via lower jaw **If lips close->use thumbs
Airway Suctioning:
Indications: remove blood/vomit/liquids/foods
Performed IMMEDIATELY when gurgling heard w spont or artificial ventilation
Promote airway patency & prevent aspiration
Complications:
Suction MAY NOT BE ADEQUATE for lrg solid obj
-use bayonet forceps
NPA’s (Nasopharyngeal airways)
Keep tongue out of airway -cant maintain headtilt long term
Insert = uncomfortable but tolerable on conscious pt
-CAN USE IF PT HAS GAG REFLEX
Rubber tube into nose -> even if airway collapse, have tube to help next steps
Indications: upper airway obstruct: awake, semi-comatose, lightly anesthetized -> facilitate airway
Facilitate NPA suctioning (suction cath down NPA) -feed tube, tumb over to suction
Clenched jaw (so ⍉ suction mouth)
Complications:                              -    epistaxis from mucosal tears or avulsions
P sores (too lrg)            -    gagging & aspiration -↓ prob since pt can gag & cough
Technique:
Measure tip of nose-earlobe/angle of mandible   -    ensure correct size (nostril)
Water-soluble lube                                               -    insert bevel toward septum
Check nasal patency -resistance=other nostril    -  deviated septum, congest, polyp
Oropharyngeal Airways: measure ear to corner of mouth -> hold tongue
Unresponsive pt -⍉ gag reflex, helps hold tongue away from back of throat
Technique:       -    measure corner of mouth-earlobe      -    scissor technique (thumb heart)
Insert backwards & rotate to “ screw into place” (rest on pt teeth)
Infants & kids use tongue depressor to lift tongue & insert oral airway right side up
Complications:
Trauma: pinch lips, ulcers (P & long contact), dental damage (fulcrum, loose teeth)
Airway hyperactivity: oropharyngeal & laryngeal reflexes triggered
Cough, retch, emesis, laryngospasm, bronchospasm, FB pushed in
Airway obstruct: ⍉placed properly/sm device->push tongue to P pharyngeal wall->obstruct
Limitations: nasal/oral airways NOT DEFINITIVE DEVICES
Manual maneuvers MUST be made a w nasal/oral airways -ensure stays open
Pt require freq suctioning to remove blood, vomit, & other secretions
Definitive devices (like ET tubes) are REQUIRED TO PROTECT AIRWAY
Ventilation Techniques
Bag-Valve Mask (BVM): self-inflating, one way valve, face mask, O2 reservoir
Most effective when connected to O2 (15L/min) -can be used w RA
[O2] supplied: -  RA -21%   -  5-10L/min O2 -40-60%   -  reservoir & 15L/min O2 -100%
Placement: narrow over nose
Technique: “E-C” thumb & index finger = C, E = fingers locking jaw
single: open airway (nasal/oral prn)->“E-C”->ventilate Q 5s-adults, 3s-peds
Incomplete seal -> chest ⍉ rise OR squeak -> wrong size
Sm hands may need to push bag against thigh
2 people: open airway (nasal/oral prn) -> 1 person 2x “E-C” -> 1person squeeze bag w 2 hands -> ventilate Q 5s-adults, 3s-peds
Stoma/tracheostomy     -    Attach BVM to tube OR peds mask over stoma for seal
Cant vent: suction stoma/tracheostomy  -    Seal mouth/nose if air escapes when vent
Infant in slightly past neutral position -
AVOID HYPEREXTENSION (block airway)
⍉EXCESSIVE VENT->gastric distension or pneumothorax->vomit
Put towel under infants shoulders to help open airway
Dentures: Be prepared to remove them
Leave in unless obviously loose -> in =preserve norm oral anatomy for ventilation
Low-Flow O2 Systems: depend on RA for pt needs, inspiratory gas flow/oxygen reservoir ⍉ meet
Dep on pt RR & depth -control in manual
Cont SpO2 monitor if on any O2
O2 above 60% w low-flow system require lrg ‘reservoir’
Nasal Cannula: 24-44% O2, 1-6L -> higher = dry nose -> epistaxis
↑ O2 by 1L/min = ↑ inspired O2 ~4% (1L =24%)
Bad O2 delivery if mouth breather
O2 can go through H2O to hydrate it if on long term
Simple Face Mask: <60% O2, 5-8L/min
[O2] dep on pt ventilatory pattern & RR -> rely on mechanical ventilation
Partial Re-Breather: 60-80%, 6-10L/min
Reservoir bag hold 600-1000mL, ensure inflated b4 you give
first ⅓ = pt exhaled vol from anatomic dead space = ↓ CO2, next breath = resivoir bag + fresh gas inhaled so ↑ [O2] in bag gas
Allows body to feel using own air (poss help stimulate natural breathing), allows to conserve O2
Non-Rebreather: 60-90%, 10-15L/min
, FULLY INFLATE B4 ON PT
3-unidirectional valves:
1./2. sides of mask-> venting exhaled gases & prevent RA enter mask on inhale
3. b/n mask & reservoir bag -prevent exhaled gas from entering bag
CPAP/BiPAP: bridge b/n intubation & non-rebreather, Pt need to coord breathing w machine
Definitive Airway : tube in trachea w inflated cuff below vocal cords
EndoTracheal Intubation (ET):
tube into trachea using BVM or ventilator   *
**ANY TUBE -GENERAL
Size = inside diameter (ID)mm, ↑ length w ↑ ID (cm marks along length)
Cuffed (adult, peds) vs uncuffed (infants)  -peds=use manometer to monitor cuff P
⍉ ATTACH BAG TOO TIGHT -> PULL OUT TUBE WHEN DETACHING
⍉ OVERINFLATE -> TRACIOMALACIA ->
P sore in trach
clean procedure,
⍉ STERILE B/C EMERGENCY
Indications:  -  Apnea   -   pre/now resp fail -tachypnea, access musc, obvious ↑ work of breathing
⍉ protect own airway (CVA, brain bleed, head injury, drugs/ETOH, stroke) -↓resp drive
Goals:
Mech patency: upper airway    -   tracheo-bronchial suction
-mucus/blood/pus
-attachment for sputum sample
Mech (+)P ventilation            -    protect from gastric -mech barrier -blood/pus/vomit
Technique:
Stay in <2Wks: tracheomalacia -> longer = tracheostomy (surgical stoma)
Stoma heal: 4wks, deep layer sutures & heals over
Complications:
-    Main stem bronchus intubation -tube into 1 lung
Soft tissue trauma/bleeding       -    Dental injury (if use teeth as fulcrum for blade)
Largyngospasm                         -    Vocal cord injury -aggressive/wrong size/inflated
Laryngeal edema from trauma   -    Hypoxia -too long, do w/in 30-45sec & pre-O2
Esophageal intubation -ausc      -
Aspiration -norm bacteria from oropharynx into trach
Equipment:
NT TUBE ⍉ GO THROUGH NPA
Oral/nasal airways         -    Lubricant (water soluble) -get through vocal cords
Diff ET tube sizes           -    Stethoscope
O2/BVM                          -    Stylet -use for all oral intubations, bend distal 1/3
10cc syringe                   -    Magill forceps (get FB out)
Pulse ox                          -    Suction -some battery operated
Laryngoscope blades/handless: pt in same position
macintosh (curved): near epiglottis, aim for vallecula, displace tongue more
miller (straight): cover epiglottis
On pt Rt -> sweep left -> cheers up, BOTH ELEVATE EPIGLOTTIS
Procedure: vocal cords after epiglottis, go ~2cm past cords
Orotracheal Intubation: Specific ET, Rt HAND PROCEDURE
Technique: Elective O.R. or Emergent    -    Need sedation: musc relaxer, anticholinergic (↓ saliva)
Position & pre-ventilate                           -    Monitor: ECG (hypoxia->arrhythmias), Pulse Ox (±95%)
Assemble & check equipment             -    pre-O2 20-120sec
Difficult airway? Automatic difficult if:
ever intubated & was hard     -    Short neck    -    Pt ⍉ open mouth 3finger width
Procedure:
****Placement: 1-2cm above carina ~22cm****
1. Tube ½ in past vocal cords (use corner of lip to measure)
2. Cont to hold tube, note location # @ lips -doc
3. Ventilated & ausc -> epigastrium & Lt/Rt chest -> equal chest rise & sounds
4. Inflate cuff 5-10cc air -> relative to tube size (can blow out cuff, but leak=wheeze)
5. Reassess tube placement -> Secure
6. Reassess tube placement & ventilation effectiveness
Success:                                     -
Pulse Ox ~97/98%
Chest rise-fall w bagged vent  -    EtCO2 waveform capnography: +5 complexes on monitor
Ausc breath sounds B/L          -
Colorimetric CO2 detector (ET adaptor)->yellow=good (+5% CO2)
Bougie stylet: conventional method -> added assurance
extra long -preloaded -> provide pathway for ET tube past vocal cords
Sensor on port to hold CO2 monitor
CXR: visualize tip of ET tube & carina.
carina ~ICS 2, T4.
ET tube=radio opaque (outline)
Necessary? -recommended, ⍉ MANDATORY if: video laryngoscope, ⍉ emergent, ↑ skilled)
Info:
Tube Size:     -    adult men: 7.5-8.5mm      -    adult women: 7-8mm
-    8mm for both
Blade Size:    -    Mac: 3-4                           -    Miller: 3
Tube Depth:   -    adult men: 23cm @teeth  -    adult women: 21cm @teeth
Positioning:
Align 3 planes =vocal cords most visible    -    TOP: trachea, oropharynx, pharynx
Sellick Maneuver (cricoid P): Use 1 finger for infant
help prevent gastric distension -> close esophagus to P<100cm/H2O
Facilitate intubation via move larynx P to bring into view
push on cricothyroid membrane  -just below thyroid cartilage
Naso-Endotracheal Intubation (NET): more difficult than oral, better tolerated by pt
Indications:
↓ TMJ mobility      -    OP repair of frx mandible
Awake                   -    Certain intra-oral & plastics procedure on head/face
Contraindications:                               -    Frx middle ⅓ of face (LeForte 3 frx)
Coagulopathy                      -    Frx base of skull
Severe intranasal patho      -    CSF (cerebral spinal fluid)  rhinorrhea
Pt Prep:
Inspect nare size & obstruction
Decongest nares via afrin spray -> cause vasoconstriction (careful w HTN pt)
Avoids epistaxis
Cocaine HCL: topical anesthetic & cause vasoconstriction
Blind Nasotracheal Intubation:
1. pt upright->tube into lrg nare->advance slow-steady
-feel resistance @turbinates->push gently past
2. Listen for sound of air mvt/whistle = tube in trachea (breath sounds through tube)
3. Advance tube -> assess placement
4. Inflate cuff -> reassess placement
5. secure -> reassess placement
Advance tube until 2cm below vocal cords
Tube Depth:   -    adult men: 26-27cm @nare  -    adult women: 24-25cm @nare
Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA): conform to hypopharynx (laryngopharynx) -lumen facing laryngeal opening
Use: is reusable, need airway for ~30min
Alt to conventional mask                      -
Pt ⍉ able to be tracheally intubated norm
latex-free                                              -    O.R.
Multi models & sizes: some inflate       -    Gaining out-of-hsp use
Indications:
Get & maintain airway control during emergent anesthetic procedures
When known or unexpected difficult airway
When multi attempts at norm intubation failed
Elective procedure where face mask used & intubation ⍉ NECESSARY
Advantages:
Easily placed   -    Few complications compare to ET or facemask anesthesia
↓ trauma          -
⍉ musc relaxant & laryngoscopy->↓musc pains & tooth damage
Parts: Port to inflate -> sit over epiglottic fold, ventilate through
Note:     -
⍉ USE W HIGH AIRWAY P
⍉ REPLACE ET TUBE
Stopped by upper esophageal sphincter
Dual Lumen Airway (DLA):
USE ONLY WHEN ⍉ ABLE TO INTUBATE BUT CAN VENTILATE
2 ports: syringe seals above & below. Look off of chest rise-fall & ausc for which one
Port 1: air through holes above inflation     -    Port 2: aire through hole below inflations
Indication: unconscious pt needs emergent airway
Contraindication:
Conscious pt    -    Pt w gag reflex
Pt >5ft tall          -    Ingest caustic->erodes=fragile->blind=damage to trach or bleed
Pt under 16y/o   -    Known esophageal dz
Insertion: blindly in center of mouth -> advance until black rings b/n teeth
Esophageal placed: 80-90%          -    endotracheal placed: 10-20%
Removal: pt start ok spont resp
1. Pt on side &
HAVE SUCTION READY
-> likely vomit
Deflate cuff #2 -> deflate cuff #1
3. Remove tube: if conscious, have pt cough while removing
4. Provide O2 & monitor for ok ventilation
Securing ET Tubes
Strap around & screw tight for long term stabilize  or tape (less secure & poss allergy)
EVERYTIME PT IS MOVED, RECHECK PLACEMENT
